newsitem.title: JAPAN: Wife identifies dead captain of Russian tanker.
newsitem.headline: Wife identifies dead captain of Russian tanker.

text.p: The wife of the Russian tanker captain who died after his ship broke up in the Sea of Japan causing Japan's worst oil spill, on Saturday formally identified her husband's body, police announced.
"Iosifovna Melnikov, 43, identified the body as her husband Valeriy Melnikov, 47, the captain of the tanker Nakhodka," a police spokesman told reporters.

Melnikov's body was found five days ago washed up on a beach near Echizen in Fukui Prefecture, 300 km (200 miles) west of Toyko. Melnikov had been missing since the tanker broke in two during a storm on January 2.
Until his wife's identification, Russian officials were unable to say positively the body was Melnikov's because of the length of time spent in the water.
The 31 other crew of the 26-year-old ship were rescued on the night of the tragedy.

The accident caused major environmental and economic havoc along a 900 kilometre (560 mile) stretch of the northwestern coastline of Honshu, Japan's main island. Three volunteers died of heart attacks during the cleanup.

Japanese foreign ministry officials said Japanese and Russian experts would meet in Moscow on Wednesday to investigate the cause of the sinking of the 13,157-tonne Nakhodka which was carrying 19,000 tonnes (133,000 barrels) of heavy oil.
The tanker broke in two 130 km (80 miles) off the coast of Shimane Prefecture.
Russian reports, unconfirmed by Japan, have said the tanker hit a half-submerged object.
Despite snowfalls, cleanup work was going on at full pace along the polluted coastline that includes rich shellfish and seaweed beds and popular tourist beaches.
